Acetaminophen pharmacology: 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient uses acetaminophen for fever and pain but expects it to strongly suppress inflammatory joint swelling. Which pharmacologic description best distinguishes its usual therapeutic profile from that of a conventional peripheral anti-inflammatory NSAID?

  1. Serious cutaneous adverse reaction
  2. Analgesic and antipyretic effects with limited peripheral anti-inflammatory action
  3. NAPQI-mediated hepatic injury
  4. N-acetylcysteine
  5. Unintentional duplicate acetaminophen exposure
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Analgesic and antipyretic effects with limited peripheral anti-inflammatory action

Acetaminophen treats pain and fever but does not provide the same peripheral anti-inflammatory action as conventional NSAIDs.

Understanding the options

Analgesic and antipyretic effects with limited peripheral anti-inflammatory action
Acetaminophen treats pain and fever but does not provide the same peripheral anti-inflammatory action as conventional NSAIDs.
NAPQI-mediated hepatic injury
Excess acetaminophen can overwhelm glutathione detoxification of the reactive metabolite NAPQI. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
N-acetylcysteine
N-acetylcysteine supports glutathione-dependent detoxification and is the antidote used for acetaminophen poisoning. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Unintentional duplicate acetaminophen exposure
Combination cold and pain products can contain acetaminophen, creating overdose risk when totals are not reconciled. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Serious cutaneous adverse reaction
Acetaminophen can rarely cause severe skin reactions, including SJS/TEN; rash with blistering or mucosal injury requires urgent assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
